featured_reviews.name: Yashvi Gavankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
After exploring multiple options for a compact yet cozy seating solution, our search for the perfect sofa led us to Durian Furniture in Thane and we couldn’t be happier. We began our journey at Godrej Interio, but their sofas didn’t quite fit our compact living room layout. Next, we visited Empire House in Bhiwandi, where the designs were undeniably premium but so were the prices, with some 2-seaters crossing ₹1 lakh even during the festive season. Even their standard 2-seater sofas were priced around ₹39,000.

While browsing online, Durian popped up as the second result after Godrej. A quick search revealed a nearby showroom, and on 4th October 2025, we decided to visit. From the moment we stepped in, the experience was refreshingly different. The showroom spans two levels: ground and first floor, offering a wide range of options. Though there’s no lift, the short climb was worth it for the variety and ambiance.

Surprisingly, a 2-seater recliner was priced lower than a standard 2-seater sofa at this store. We ended up choosing a fabric manual recliner named Canyon for ₹44,500 just slightly more than Empire’s basic sofa, and that too with the added comfort and functionality of a recliner. The festive Diwali discount made the deal even sweeter. Most sofas were available at a generous 50% discount, and select models could be customized. Custom orders typically take about a month to deliver, while ready models arrive within 7–8 days. The tactile experience made a huge difference, something online browsing just can’t replicate.

Raj Sir was incredibly helpful, patiently walking us through options that matched both our budget and space constraints. He explained the pros and cons of fabric vs. leather recliners, and manual vs. motorized mechanisms, helping us make an informed choice. The store also houses a premium collection, including Italian leather pieces that exude luxury.

Durian Furniture in Thane offers a thoughtful blend of affordability, aesthetics, and expert service. I highly recommend this place for furniture buying.

featured_reviews.name: Paresh Koli
featured_reviews.review_text:
Searching for furniture for my 2BHK in Mahalaxmi, I considered several options after dismissing high quotes from interior decorators. I chose A F Furniture from four shortlisted vendors, despite them giving the second-highest quote, because their work looked impressive on Instagram videos.

The initial WhatsApp quote from the owner, Irfan bhai, based on my measurements was 5.5 lakhs. However, after he personally inspected the site and confirmed using good MR grade ply, laminate, and branded mechanisms like Hettich, the price increased to 9 lakhs, which was negotiated down to 8.5 lakhs. A condition of the contract was pre-making the furniture in the warehouse to minimize on-site work and avoid a large housing society deposit for exceeding 10 days. While Irfan bhai agreed to a 4-5 day on-site assembly, it ultimately took 7-8 days. Additionally, workers often did not arrive on time, requiring communication. The assembly started with 6-7 workers but quickly reduced to 1-3 per day, necessitating active monitoring to prevent damage to the house.

Positives:
Owner Irfan bhai is a nice, humble, and soft-spoken person.
Prices were decent, though not the best available.
Overall quality of work was decent.
Negatives:

Damages & Cost
Workers broke the tempered glass of the guest bedroom with a large crack (repair costing upwards of 1 lakh, which they refused responsibility for). Also, huge scratches were put in the wooden flooring during installation, ruining the look of the room.

Quality & Materials/Workmanship
There are many small defects in craftsmanship, including laminates chipping off the edges during installation and within the first two months, laminate coming off inside a wardrobe, and sharp edges that caused multiple cuts. Despite a promise of good quality MR grade ply without gaps, almost half the furniture uses poor quality ply with gaps, which they blamed on the manufacturer. They used jhatpat glue instead of Fevicol, and the laminate sides are separating in many places. The sliding wardrobe mechanism was initially a non-branded one they falsely insisted was Hettich; after replacement, the doors are too close and brush together, causing marks on the laminate. Their machines are ordinary and not modern; for example, they initially refused to install the Hettich kitchen sliding door, requiring me to contact Hettich customer care for instruction. Finesse was missing in the final grooving for this door. Laminate was also omitted from the wall end and back of the temple unit, which required a follow-up call to install the side laminate.

Design & Service Flaws
Several items had design and sizing issues: one master bedroom sofa cum bed was too large due to 8-inch hand rests, and the replacement still has uncovered, painful areas. A single sofa cum bed had huge handles that didn't account for room size; after removing the handles to fit, the side panel remains uncovered and looks "pathetic," which they refused to fix due to transportation costs. TV bottom units were made without considering socket locations, requiring makeshift installations. The rotating shoe rack mechanism was unusable for adult shoes, forcing a replacement with a routine door type (which they charged for). Furthermore, I had to pay 15k extra and follow up for weeks for extra wardrobe shelves that were promised for free. Workers frequently claimed they could not perform simple tasks that I had to do myself (like removing wood from a cupboard or door alignment), which would have cost 5-10k extra if I hadn't been a DIY person. Dining table seat cushions are too large for the bench space and are unusable.

Verdict:
The work offers decent value for money, but poor finishing, evident cost-cutting measures, and ordinary after-sales service are significant red flags that prospective clients should consider and clarify before engaging A F Furniture.
